caption: Khalil v. President
citation_line: Khalil v. President, 777 F. Supp. 3d 369 (D.N.J. 2025); appeal, Nos. 25-2162 & 25-2357 (3d Cir. Jan. 15, 2026)
headnote_district_ruling: Judge Farbiarz held that the District of New Jersey could hear Mahmoud Khalil’s habeas petition after his rapid interstate transfers, preliminarily enjoined removal on a foreign-policy ground, and later ordered release from detention.
qualification_rationale: The case drew intense national attention and raised first-order questions about habeas geography, immediate-custodian rules, First Amendment retaliation and the INA’s channeling of removal-related review.
appellate_posture_note: A divided precedential Third Circuit panel agreed that the New Jersey court had habeas jurisdiction as the district of confinement, but held that 8 U.S.C. § 1252(b)(9) stripped subject-matter jurisdiction over the removal-related claims. It vacated the challenged orders and remanded with instructions to dismiss without reaching the constitutional merits. Rehearing en banc was denied on May 22, 2026; the mandate was stayed pending a certiorari petition. Supreme Court docket No. 26A90 extended the petition deadline to September 21, 2026; no petition was shown on the docket by the September 10 cutoff.
